source.title: Letter 344
source.breadcrumbs: Home > Fathers of the Church > Letters (St. Basil of Caesarea) > Letter 344

paragraphs.text: I am dissuaded from writing often to you, learned as you are, by my timidity and my ignorance. But your persistent silence is different. What excuse can be offered for it? If any one takes into account that you are slow to write to me, living as you do in the midst of letters, he will condemn you for forgetfulness of me. He who is ready at speaking is not unprepared to write. And if a man so endowed is silent, it is plain that he acts either from forgetfulness or from contempt. I will, however, requite your silence with a greeting. Farewell, most honoured sir. Write if you like. If you prefer it, do not write.

latex.p0004: 我因怯懦和无知，不敢经常写信给像你这样有学问的人。但你的持久沉默则是另一回事。这有什么借口可言呢？如果有人考虑到你生活在文字之中，却很少写信给我，他将责备你忘记了我。一个善于说话的人，并不是不擅长写作。如果一个这样有天赋的人保持沉默，显然他的行为出于忘记或轻视。然而，我将以问候来回报你的沉默。再见，尊贵的阁下。如果你喜欢，就写信。如果你更喜欢，就不要写。
